name: Infectious Disease with Peripheral Neuropathy

criteria.description: Presence of clinical signs and symptoms consistent with peripheral neuropathy including sensory and/or motor deficits
Laboratory or microbiological evidence of an infectious agent known to cause neuropathy
Electrodiagnostic studies confirming peripheral nerve involvement
Exclusion of other common causes of peripheral neuropathy such as diabetes, toxins, or hereditary neuropathies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: clinical neuropathy, evidence of infectious agent, and electrodiagnostic confirmation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of other neuropathy etiologies and correlation with infectious disease history or testing.

searchTerms: loss of feeling in hands and feet
pins and needles in distal extremities
weak muscles in hands and feet
loss of strength in distal limbs
muscle weakness in arms and legs
problems with facial and head nerves
nerve issues affecting face and head

occasional.symptomName: Neuropathic pain with burning or shooting quality
searchTerms: tingling burning pain in arms or legs
mild problems with balance and coordination
impaired coordination due to sensory loss
difficulty breathing due to muscle weakness

rare.symptomName: Severe autonomic failure with urinary retention
searchTerms: loss of autonomic control with bladder problems

laboratory: Positive serology or PCR for infectious agents (e.g., HIV, Hepatitis C, Lyme disease)
Elevated inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) in some cases
CSF analysis may show elevated protein without pleocytosis
imaging: MRI may show nerve root or plexus enhancement in some cases
Ultrasound of peripheral nerves may reveal enlargement or hypoechogenicity
genetic: No specific genetic markers; genetic testing used to exclude hereditary neuropathies
other: Nerve biopsy may show inflammatory infiltrates or vasculitis
Electrodiagnostic studies demonstrate demyelination or axonal loss

distinguishingFeatures: Symmetric distal neuropathy without infectious markers
Genetic testing positive for causative mutations
Chronic progressive course without infectious etiology

redFlags: Severe autonomic instability (e.g., arrhythmias, urinary retention)
references: Dyck PJ, Thomas PK. Peripheral Neuropathy. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2005.
Hughes RA, Cornblath DR. Guillain-Barré syndrome. Lancet. 2005 Nov 5;366(9497):1653-66.
